summary: Beall Woods State Park is an Illinois state park bordering the Wabash River and Keensburg in Wabash County. Its core is an old-growth hardwood forest designated a state Natural Area, and portions are a National Natural Landmark called the Forest of the Wabash. The park was created in 1966 and offers a small primitive campground, a visitor center opened in April 2001, and hiking trails.
one_line: Beall Woods State Park is an Illinois state park on the Wabash River with old-growth hardwood forest and a National Natural Landmark.
key_facts: Beall Woods State Park is an Illinois state park bordering the Wabash River and Keensburg in Wabash County, Illinois.
The park's old-growth forest is designated a "Natural Area" by the state of Illinois.
The trees in the forest consist overwhelmingly of hardwoods of the former Eastern Woodlands ecosystem.
Portions of Beall Woods State Park have been designated a National Natural Landmark as the "Forest of the Wabash".
The state park was created in 1966.
The nearest towns with sizable commercial infrastructure, including hotels and grocery stores, are Grayville and Mount Carmel.
Beall Woods State Park hosts a small primitive campground.
Beall Woods State Park maintains a visitor center which opened in April 2001.
The park maintains hiking trails, primarily through the Forest of the Wabash portion of the park.
